title: Bengaluru fitness app fixed free-to-paid churn with a WhatsApp Day-1-to-3 habit loop — paid base grew 2.4x on flat ad spend
content: A Bengaluru fitness-and-nutrition app was buying 38,000 free installs/month at ₹47 CAC across Meta, Google and YouTube, but only 2.1% converted to the ₹499/month plan and 61% of those paid users churned inside 60 days. The founders blamed pricing; the data blamed Day 2-3 drop-off — 72% of installs never logged a second workout or a single meal. So I froze top-funnel spend and rebuilt the first 72 hours. We moved trial onboarding onto a WhatsApp Business loop (opt-in at signup, 71% open rate vs email's 9%): Day-1 a 5-minute starter workout, Day-2 a desi meal card (roti-sabzi macros, not quinoa), Day-3 a 'log your streak' nudge answered by a human coach. The 7-day trial was gated behind one logged workout, and we added a ₹299 quarterly tier for tier-2/3 users priced for UPI wallets. Over 11 weeks Day-7 activation rose 28%→49%, free-to-paid hit 4.6%, and 60-day churn fell 61%→34%. The paying base grew 2.4x on identical ad spend; blended CAC-to-paid dropped from ₹2,238 to ₹1,021.
lesson: When free-to-paid is broken, fix activation before you touch pricing or buy more installs — the first 72 hours, not the price tag, decide retention. In India a WhatsApp onboarding loop (71% open) carrying localized desi content plus a single 'one logged action' gate converts intent into habit far cheaper than renting more top-funnel traffic.
